title: Chicken Marsala
subtitle: Sautéed chicken in Marsala wine and mushroom sauce
excerpt: Flattened chicken breasts sautéed until golden then finished in a quick pan sauce of Marsala wine, chicken stock, and mushrooms. An Italian-American classic that comes together in twenty minutes with any good fortified wine.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chicken Marsala is an Italian-American dish rather than an Italian one; it emerged from the Italian immigrant community in the United States in the late nineteenth and early twentieth century and became popular in Italian-American restaurants. It uses Marsala wine from Sicily, which is a fortified wine with a distinctive caramel and nut flavour that makes an outstanding pan sauce without lengthy reduction. The dish is related to Italian piccata and scaloppine preparations, which also use flattened, sautéed chicken or veal with a fast pan sauce, but Marsala's sweetness is distinctive. The technique is the same as for all scaloppine: the meat must be pounded thin so it cooks quickly and evenly; the fond from the sear is the base of the sauce.

content.text: Pound the chicken between two sheets of cling film to an even 1 cm thickness. Uneven pieces cook unevenly: the thick parts stay raw while the thin parts dry out. The pan must be very hot when the chicken goes in so it colours rather than steams.

items.preparation: use 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts; pounded to 1 cm thickness

content.text: Season the chicken breasts and dust lightly in flour, shaking off the excess. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over high heat. Sear the chicken for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Remove and keep warm.

Add half the butter to the pan. Cook the shallot and mushrooms over medium-high heat for 5 minutes until the mushrooms are golden and any liquid has evaporated. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.

Pour in the Marsala and let it bubble and reduce by half, scraping up any browned bits. Add the chicken stock and reduce by half again, about 3 minutes. Remove from the heat and stir in the remaining butter to make the sauce glossy. Return the chicken to the pan, turning to coat. Serve scattered with parsley.
